At both Terminal 1 and Terminal 2, the taxi stands are right outside the arrivals hall on the 1st floor. There are separate stands for regular taxis, deluxe (mobeom) taxis and jumbo taxis, and also separate lines for Seoul and for Incheon/Gyeonggi-do.
Fares are metered, and a ride to Seoul City Hall costs around KRW 57,000–71,000 (estimated from fares as of November 2026). From 22:00–4:00, a late-night surcharge of 20–40% applies.
Do not get into unlicensed cars offered by touts who approach you in the arrivals hall. The surest way to give your destination is to show the driver your hotel name and its address in Korean.
If you want to book a taxi
You normally don't need to book a taxi, but if you arrive late at night, travel in a large group, or want to arrange things in Japanese, a pre-booked transfer gives you more peace of mind.

Kuma Travel's Incheon Airport transfer costs a flat KRW 150,000 to anywhere in central Seoul (Staria, up to 6 passengers, 1 vehicle). The price stays the same late at night, early in the morning or in traffic, and round-trip bookings get 10% off.
Your driver waits at the arrivals hall exit holding a sign with your name. We track flight delays ourselves, so there is no extra charge.

Many people search by hotel name, and directions to Lotte Hotel Seoul and Noblesse Hotel are common searches. Whatever your hotel, just send us its name or address and we'll take you to the front entrance.
